<span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="Seal of the President of the United States" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States.svg/70px-Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States.svg.png" decoding="async" width="70" height="70" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States.svg/105px-Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States.svg/140px-Seal_of_the_President_of_the_United_States.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="2424" data-file-height="2425" /></span></span></td>
</tr><tr><td class="sidebar-navbar"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1129693374"><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1063604349">.mw-parser-output .navbar{display:inline;font-size:88%;font-weight:normal}.mw-parser-output .navbar-collapse{float:left;text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .navbar-boxtext{word-spacing:0}.mw-parser-output .navbar ul{display:inline-block;white-space:nowrap;line-height:inherit}.mw-parser-output .navbar-brackets::before{margin-right:-0.125em;content:"[ "}.mw-parser-output .navbar-brackets::after{margin-left:-0.125em;content:" ]"}.mw-parser-output .navbar li{word-spacing:-0.125em}.mw-parser-output .navbar a>span,.mw-parser-output .navbar a>abbr{text-decoration:inherit}.mw-parser-output .navbar-mini abbr{font-variant:small-caps;border-bottom:none;text-decoration:none;cursor:inherit}.mw-parser-output .navbar-ct-full{font-size:114%;margin:0 7em}.mw-parser-output .navbar-ct-mini{font-size:114%;margin:0 4em}</style><div class="navbar plainlinks hlist navbar-mini"><ul><li class="nv-view"><a href="/wiki/Template:Donald_Trump_series" title="Template:Donald Trump series"><abbr title="View this template">v</abbr></a></li><li class="nv-talk"><a href="/wiki/Template_talk:Donald_Trump_series" title="Template talk:Donald Trump series"><abbr title="Discuss this template">t</abbr></a></li><li class="nv-edit"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Donald_Trump_series&amp;action=edit"><abbr title="Edit this template">e</abbr></a></li></ul></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><b>Donald John Trump</b> (born June 14, 1946) is an American politician, media personality, and businessman who served as the 45th <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_United_States" title="President of the United States">president of the United States</a> from 2017 to 2021.
</p><p>Trump graduated from the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania" title="University of Pennsylvania">University of Pennsylvania</a> with a bachelor's degree in economics in 1968. He became president of his father's real-estate business in 1971 and renamed it the <a href="/wiki/Trump_Organization" class="mw-redirect" title="Trump Organization">Trump Organization</a>. He expanded its operations to building and renovating skyscrapers, hotels, casinos, and golf courses and later started side ventures, mostly by licensing his name. From 2004 to 2015, he co-produced and hosted the reality television series <i><a href="/wiki/The_Apprentice_(American_TV_series)" title="The Apprentice (American TV series)">The Apprentice</a></i>. He and his businesses have been plaintiff or defendant in more than 4,000 state and federal legal actions, including six business bankruptcies.
</p><p>Trump won the <a href="/wiki/2016_U.S._presidential_election" class="mw-redirect" title="2016 U.S. presidential election">2016 presidential election</a> as the Republican nominee against Democratic nominee <a href="/wiki/Hillary_Clinton" title="Hillary Clinton">Hillary Clinton</a> while losing the popular vote.<sup id="cite_ref-electoral-college_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-electoral-college-1">&#91;a&#93;</a></sup> During the campaign, his political positions were described as populist, protectionist, isolationist, and nationalist. His election and policies sparked numerous protests. He was the first U.S. president with no prior military or government service. The <a href="/wiki/Mueller_special_counsel_investigation" title="Mueller special counsel investigation">2017–2019 special counsel investigation</a> established that <a href="/wiki/Russian_interference_in_the_2016_United_States_elections" title="Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections">Russia interfered in the 2016 election</a> to favor his campaign. Trump promoted conspiracy theories and made many false and misleading statements during his campaigns and presidency, to a degree unprecedented in American politics. Many of his comments and actions have been characterized as racially charged or racist and many as misogynistic.
</p><p>As president, Trump <a href="/wiki/Executive_Order_13769" title="Executive Order 13769">ordered a travel ban</a> on citizens from several Muslim-majority countries, diverted military funding toward building a wall on the U.S.-Mexico border, and implemented a <a href="/wiki/Trump_administration_family_separation_policy" title="Trump administration family separation policy">policy of family separations</a> for apprehended migrants. He weakened environmental protections, rolling back more than 100 environmental policies and regulations. He signed the <a href="/wiki/Tax_Cuts_and_Jobs_Act_of_2017" class="mw-redirect" title="Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017">Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017</a>, which cut taxes for individuals and businesses and rescinded the <a href="/wiki/Health_insurance_mandate" title="Health insurance mandate">individual health insurance mandate</a> penalty of the <a href="/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act" title="Affordable Care Act">Affordable Care Act</a>. He appointed <a href="/wiki/Neil_Gorsuch" title="Neil Gorsuch">Neil Gorsuch</a>, <a href="/wiki/Brett_Kavanaugh" title="Brett Kavanaugh">Brett Kavanaugh</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Amy_Coney_Barrett" title="Amy Coney Barrett">Amy Coney Barrett</a> to the U.S. Supreme Court. He initiated a trade war with China and withdrew the U.S. from the proposed <a href="/wiki/Trans-Pacific_Partnership" title="Trans-Pacific Partnership">Trans-Pacific Partnership</a> trade agreement, the <a href="/wiki/Paris_Agreement" title="Paris Agreement">Paris Agreement</a> on climate change, and the <a href="/wiki/Iran_nuclear_deal" class="mw-redirect" title="Iran nuclear deal">Iran nuclear deal</a>. He met with North Korean leader <a href="/wiki/Kim_Jong_Un" title="Kim Jong Un">Kim Jong Un</a> three times but made no progress on denuclearization. He reacted slowly to the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States" title="COVID-19 pandemic in the United States">COVID-19 pandemic</a>, ignored or contradicted many recommendations from health officials, used political pressure to interfere with testing efforts, and spread misinformation about unproven treatments.
</p><p>Trump lost the <a href="/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election" title="2020 United States presidential election">2020 presidential election</a> to <a href="/wiki/Joe_Biden" title="Joe Biden">Joe Biden</a>. He refused to concede defeat, falsely claiming widespread electoral fraud, and <a href="/wiki/Attempts_to_overturn_the_2020_United_States_presidential_election" title="Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election">attempted to overturn the results</a> by pressuring government officials, mounting scores of unsuccessful legal challenges, and obstructing the presidential transition. On January 6, 2021, he urged his supporters to march to the <a href="/wiki/U.S._Capitol" class="mw-redirect" title="U.S. Capitol">U.S. Capitol</a>, which many of them then <a href="/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack" title="January 6 United States Capitol attack">attacked</a>, resulting in multiple deaths and interrupting the electoral vote count.
</p><p>Trump is the only American president to have been impeached twice. After he tried to pressure Ukraine in 2019 to investigate Biden, he was impeached in December by the <a href="/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives" title="United States House of Representatives">House of Representatives</a> for abuse of power and obstruction of Congress; he was acquitted by the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Senate" title="United States Senate">Senate</a> in February 2020. The House impeached him a second time in January 2021, for incitement of insurrection, and the Senate acquitted him the next month. Scholars and historians <a href="/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States" title="Historical rankings of presidents of the United States">rank Trump</a> as one of the worst presidents in American history.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2">&#91;1&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-scri_22_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scri_22-3">&#91;2&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Since leaving office, Trump has remained heavily involved in the Republican Party. In November 2022, he announced his candidacy for the Republican nomination in the <a href="/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election" title="2024 United States presidential election">2024 presidential election</a>. In March 2023, a <a href="/wiki/Prosecution_of_Donald_Trump_in_New_York" title="Prosecution of Donald Trump in New York">Manhattan grand jury indicted</a> him on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records. In June, a <a href="/wiki/Federal_prosecution_of_Donald_Trump_(classified_documents_case)" title="Federal prosecution of Donald Trump (classified documents case)">Miami federal grand jury indicted</a> him on 37 felonies related to his <a href="/wiki/FBI_investigation_into_Donald_Trump%27s_handling_of_government_documents" title="FBI investigation into Donald Trump&#39;s handling of government documents">handling of classified documents</a> (with three charges added in July). In August, a <a href="/wiki/Federal_prosecution_of_Donald_Trump_(election_obstruction_case)" title="Federal prosecution of Donald Trump (election obstruction case)">Washington, D.C., federal grand jury indicted</a> him on four felony counts of conspiracy and obstruction related to efforts to overturn the 2020 election. Later in August, a <a href="/wiki/Georgia_election_racketeering_prosecution" title="Georgia election racketeering prosecution">Fulton County, Georgia, grand jury indicted him</a> for racketeering and other felonies committed in an effort to overturn the state's 2020 election results. Trump pleaded not guilty to all charges. 
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r886046785">.mw-parser-output .toclimit-2 .toclevel-1 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-3 .toclevel-2 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-4 .toclevel-3 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-5 .toclevel-4 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-6 .toclevel-5 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-7 .toclevel-6 ul{display:none}</style><div class="toclimit-4"><meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" /></div>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Personal_life">Personal life</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_life">Early life</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="A black-and-white photograph of Donald Trump as a teenager, smiling, wearing a dark pseudo-military uniform with various badges and a light-colored stripe crossing his right shoulder" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg/150px-Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg" decoding="async" width="150" height="197" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg/225px-Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg/300px-Donald_Trump_NYMA.jpg 2x" data-file-width="780" data-file-height="1024" /></a><figcaption>Trump at the <a href="/wiki/New_York_Military_Academy" title="New York Military Academy">New York Military Academy</a> in 1964</figcaption></figure>
<p>Donald John Trump was born on June 14, 1946, at <a href="/wiki/Jamaica_Hospital_Medical_Center" title="Jamaica Hospital Medical Center">Jamaica Hospital</a> in <a href="/wiki/Queens" title="Queens">Queens</a>, New York City,<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4">&#91;3&#93;</a></sup> the fourth child of <a href="/wiki/Fred_Trump" title="Fred Trump">Fred Trump</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Bronx" class="mw-redirect" title="Bronx">Bronx</a>-born real-estate developer whose parents were German immigrants, and <a href="/wiki/Mary_Anne_MacLeod_Trump" title="Mary Anne MacLeod Trump">Mary Anne MacLeod Trump</a>, an immigrant from Scotland. Trump grew up with older siblings <a href="/wiki/Maryanne_Trump_Barry" title="Maryanne Trump Barry">Maryanne</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fred_Trump_Jr." title="Fred Trump Jr.">Fred Jr.</a>, and Elizabeth and younger brother <a href="/wiki/Robert_Trump" title="Robert Trump">Robert</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Jamaica_Estates,_Queens" title="Jamaica Estates, Queens">Jamaica Estates</a> neighborhood of Queens, and attended the private <a href="/wiki/Kew-Forest_School" title="Kew-Forest School">Kew-Forest School</a> from kindergarten through seventh grade.<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5">&#91;4&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA33_33&#93;_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA33_33]-6">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> At age 13, he was enrolled at the <a href="/wiki/New_York_Military_Academy" title="New York Military Academy">New York Military Academy</a>, a private boarding school,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA38_38&#93;_8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA38_38]-8">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup> and, in 1964, he enrolled at <a href="/wiki/Fordham_University" title="Fordham University">Fordham University</a>. Two years later, he transferred to the <a href="/wiki/Wharton_School_of_the_University_of_Pennsylvania" class="mw-redirect" title="Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania">Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania</a>, graduating in May 1968 with a <a href="/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science" title="Bachelor of Science">Bachelor of Science</a> in economics.<sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, Trump's lawyer <a href="/wiki/Michael_Cohen_(lawyer)" title="Michael Cohen (lawyer)">Michael Cohen</a> threatened Trump's colleges, high school, and the <a href="/wiki/College_Board" title="College Board">College Board</a> with legal action if they released Trump's academic records.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>While in college, Trump obtained four student <a href="/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States" title="Conscription in the United States">draft</a> deferments during the <a href="/wiki/Vietnam_War" title="Vietnam War">Vietnam War</a> era.<sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12">&#91;11&#93;</a></sup> In 1966, he was deemed fit for military service based upon a medical examination, and in July 1968, a local draft board classified him as eligible to serve.<sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13">&#91;12&#93;</a></sup> In October 1968, he was classified <span class="nowrap">1-Y</span>, a conditional medical deferment,<sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup> and in 1972, he was reclassified <span class="nowrap">4-F</span> due to <a href="/wiki/Bone_spurs" class="mw-redirect" title="Bone spurs">bone spurs</a>, permanently disqualifying him from service.<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Family">Family</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Family_of_Donald_Trump" title="Family of Donald Trump">Family of Donald Trump</a></div>
<p>In 1977, Trump married <a href="/wiki/Czechs" title="Czechs">Czech</a> model <a href="/wiki/Ivana_Zeln%C3%AD%C4%8Dkov%C3%A1" class="mw-redirect" title="Ivana Zelníčková">Ivana Zelníčková</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBlair2015300_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2015300-16">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup> They had three children: <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump_Jr." title="Donald Trump Jr.">Donald Jr.</a> (born 1977), <a href="/wiki/Ivanka_Trump" title="Ivanka Trump">Ivanka</a> (born 1981), and <a href="/wiki/Eric_Trump" title="Eric Trump">Eric</a> (born 1984). Ivana became a <a href="/wiki/Citizenship_of_the_United_States" title="Citizenship of the United States">naturalized United States citizen</a> in 1988.<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> The couple divorced in 1990, following Trump's affair with actress <a href="/wiki/Marla_Maples" title="Marla Maples">Marla Maples</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup> Trump and Maples married in 1993 and divorced in 1999. They have one daughter, <a href="/wiki/Tiffany_Trump" title="Tiffany Trump">Tiffany</a> (born 1993), who was raised by Marla in California.<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup> In 2005, Trump married Slovenian model <a href="/wiki/Melania_Knauss" class="mw-redirect" title="Melania Knauss">Melania Knauss</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup> They have one son, Barron (born 2006).<sup id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup> Melania gained U.S. citizenship in 2006.<sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<p>Trump went to <a href="/wiki/Sunday_school" title="Sunday school">Sunday school</a> and was <a href="/wiki/Confirmation" title="Confirmation">confirmed</a> in 1959 at the <a href="/wiki/First_Presbyterian_Church_in_Jamaica" title="First Presbyterian Church in Jamaica">First Presbyterian Church in Jamaica</a>, Queens.<sup id="cite_ref-BarronNYT_23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BarronNYT-23">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-inactive_24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inactive-24">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> In the 1970s, his parents joined the <a href="/wiki/Marble_Collegiate_Church" title="Marble Collegiate Church">Marble Collegiate Church</a> in Manhattan, which belongs to the <a href="/wiki/Reformed_Church_in_America" title="Reformed Church in America">Reformed Church in America</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-BarronNYT_23-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BarronNYT-23">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-WaPo.March.18.17_25-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WaPo.March.18.17-25">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup> The pastor at Marble, <a href="/wiki/Norman_Vincent_Peale" title="Norman Vincent Peale">Norman Vincent Peale</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-BarronNYT_23-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BarronNYT-23">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup> ministered to the family until his death in 1993.<sup id="cite_ref-WaPo.March.18.17_25-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WaPo.March.18.17-25">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup> Trump has described him as a mentor.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA81_81&#93;_26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA81_81]-26">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, the church stated that Trump was not an active member.<sup id="cite_ref-inactive_24-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inactive-24">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> In 2019, he appointed his personal pastor, televangelist <a href="/wiki/Paula_White" title="Paula White">Paula White</a>, to the White House <a href="/wiki/Office_of_Public_Liaison" title="Office of Public Liaison">Office of Public Liaison</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup> In 2020, he said he identified as a <a href="/wiki/Non-denominational_Christian" class="mw-redirect" title="Non-denominational Christian">non-denominational Christian</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Health_habits">Health habits</span></h3>
<p>Trump has called golfing his "primary form of exercise" but usually does not walk the course.<sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup> He considers exercise a waste of energy because he believes exercise depletes the body's energy "like a battery, with a finite amount of energy".<sup id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, Trump's campaign released a letter from his longtime personal physician, <a href="/wiki/Harold_Bornstein" title="Harold Bornstein">Harold Bornstein</a>, stating that Trump would "be the healthiest individual ever elected to the presidency".<sup id="cite_ref-dictation_31-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dictation-31">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, Bornstein said Trump had dictated the contents of the letter and that three Trump agents had seized his medical records in a February 2017 raid on the doctor's office.<sup id="cite_ref-dictation_31-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dictation-31">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Wealth">Wealth</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Wealth_of_Donald_Trump" title="Wealth of Donald Trump">Wealth of Donald Trump</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Ivana Trump and King Fahd shake hands, with Ronald Reagan standing next to them smiling. All are in black formal attire." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg/260px-Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg" decoding="async" width="260" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg/390px-Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg/520px-Ivana_Trump_shakes_hands_with_Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="2885" /></a><figcaption>Trump (far right) and wife Ivana in the receiving line of a state dinner for King <a href="/wiki/Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia" title="Fahd of Saudi Arabia">Fahd of Saudi Arabia</a> in 1985, with U.S. president <a href="/wiki/Ronald_Reagan" title="Ronald Reagan">Ronald Reagan</a> and First Lady <a href="/wiki/Nancy_Reagan" title="Nancy Reagan">Nancy Reagan</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1982, Trump made the initial <i><a href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</a></i> list of wealthy people for holding a share of his family's estimated $200&#160;million net worth (equivalent to $606&#160;million in 2022).<sup id="cite_ref-inflation-US_33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inflation-US-33">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> His losses in the 1980s dropped him from the list between 1990 and 1995.<sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup> After filing the mandatory financial disclosure report with the <a href="/wiki/Federal_Election_Commission" title="Federal Election Commission">FEC</a> in July 2015, he announced a net worth of about $10&#160;billion. Records released by the FEC showed at least $1.4&#160;billion in assets and $265&#160;million in liabilities.<sup id="cite_ref-disclosure_35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-disclosure-35">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup> <i>Forbes</i> estimated his net worth dropped by $1.4&#160;billion between 2015 and 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup> In their 2021 billionaires ranking, Trump's net worth was estimated to be $2.4&#160;billion (1,299th in the world).<sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Journalist Jonathan Greenberg reported that Trump called him in 1984, pretending to be a fictional Trump Organization official named "<a href="/wiki/John_Barron_(pseudonym)" class="mw-redirect" title="John Barron (pseudonym)">John Barron</a>". Greenberg said that Trump, speaking as "Barron", falsely asserted that he owned more than 90 percent of his father's business to get a higher ranking for himself on the <a href="/wiki/Forbes_400" title="Forbes 400"><i>Forbes</i> 400</a> list of wealthy Americans. Greenberg also wrote that <i>Forbes</i> had vastly overestimated Trump's wealth and wrongly included him on the <i>Forbes</i> 400 rankings of 1982, 1983, and 1984.<sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Trump has often said he began his career with "a small loan of one million dollars" from his father and that he had to pay it back with interest.<sup id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup> He was a millionaire by age eight, borrowed at least $60&#160;million from his father, largely failed to repay those loans, and received another $413&#160;million (adjusted for inflation) from his father's company.<sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Tax_Schemes_41-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tax_Schemes-41">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, he and his family were reported to have committed tax fraud, and the <a href="/wiki/New_York_State_Department_of_Taxation_and_Finance" title="New York State Department of Taxation and Finance">New York State Department of Taxation and Finance</a> started an investigation.<sup id="cite_ref-Tax_Schemes_41-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tax_Schemes-41">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup> His investments underperformed the stock and New York property markets.<sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup> <i>Forbes</i> estimated in October 2018 that his net worth declined from $4.5&#160;billion in 2015 to $3.1&#160;billion in 2017 and his product-licensing income from $23&#160;million to $3&#160;million.<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Contrary to his claims of financial health and business acumen, <a href="/wiki/Tax_returns_of_Donald_Trump" title="Tax returns of Donald Trump">Trump's tax returns</a> from 1985 to 1994 show net losses totaling $1.17&#160;billion. The losses were higher than those of almost every other American taxpayer. The losses in 1990 and 1991, more than $250&#160;million each year, were more than double those of the nearest taxpayers. In 1995, his reported losses were $915.7&#160;million (equivalent to $1.76&#160;billion in 2022).<sup id="cite_ref-Buettner-190508_45-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buettner-190508-45">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-inflation-US_33-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inflation-US-33">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2020, the <i>New York Times</i> obtained Trump's tax information extending over two decades. Its reporters found that Trump reported losses of hundreds of millions of dollars and had, since 2010, deferred declaring $287&#160;million in forgiven debt as taxable income. His income mainly came from his share in <i><a href="/wiki/The_Apprentice_(American_TV_series)" title="The Apprentice (American TV series)">The Apprentice</a></i> and businesses in which he was a minority partner, and his losses mainly from majority-owned businesses. Much income was in <a href="/wiki/Tax_credit" title="Tax credit">tax credits</a> for his losses, which let him avoid annual income tax payments or lower them to $750. During the 2010s, Trump balanced his businesses' losses by selling and borrowing against assets, including a $100&#160;million mortgage on <a href="/wiki/Trump_Tower" title="Trump Tower">Trump Tower</a> (due in 2022) and the liquidation of over $200&#160;million in stocks and bonds. He personally guaranteed $421&#160;million in debt, most of which is due by 2024.<sup id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As of October 2021, Trump had over $1.3&#160;billion in total debts, much of which is secured by his assets.<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup> In 2020, he owed $640&#160;million to banks and trust organizations, including <a href="/wiki/Bank_of_China" title="Bank of China">Bank of China</a>, <a href="/wiki/Deutsche_Bank" title="Deutsche Bank">Deutsche Bank</a>, and <a href="/wiki/UBS" title="UBS">UBS</a>, and approximately $450&#160;million to unknown creditors. The value of his assets exceeds his debt.<sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Business_career">Business career</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Business_career_of_Donald_Trump" title="Business career of Donald Trump">Business career of Donald Trump</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Business_projects_of_Donald_Trump_in_Russia" title="Business projects of Donald Trump in Russia">Business projects of Donald Trump in Russia</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Real_estate">Real estate</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Exterior ground view of Trump tower, a contemporary skyscraper with a glass curtain and stepped façade" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg/170px-Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="227" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg/255px-Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg/340px-Trump_Tower_-_lower_part.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2448" data-file-height="3264" /></a><figcaption>Trump Tower in <a href="/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan" title="Midtown Manhattan">Midtown Manhattan</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Starting in 1968, Trump was employed at his father Fred's real-estate company, Trump Management, which owned middle-class rental housing in New York City's outer boroughs.<sup id="cite_ref-Mahler_50-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mahler-50">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Rich_NYMag_51-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rich_NYMag-51">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup> In 1971, he became president of the company and began using the <a href="/wiki/Trump_Organization" class="mw-redirect" title="Trump Organization">Trump Organization</a> as an <a href="/wiki/Umbrella_brand" title="Umbrella brand">umbrella brand</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBlair2015&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksiduJifCgAAQBAJpgPA250_250&#93;_52-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2015[httpsbooksgooglecombooksiduJifCgAAQBAJpgPA250_250]-52">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup> Between 1991 and 2009, he filed for <a href="/wiki/Chapter_11" class="mw-redirect" title="Chapter 11">Chapter 11</a> bankruptcy protection for six of his businesses, the <a href="/wiki/Plaza_Hotel" title="Plaza Hotel">Plaza Hotel</a> in Manhattan, the casinos in <a href="/wiki/Atlantic_City,_New_Jersey" title="Atlantic City, New Jersey">Atlantic City, New Jersey</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Trump_Hotels_%26_Casino_Resorts" class="mw-redirect" title="Trump Hotels &amp; Casino Resorts">Trump Hotels &amp; Casino Resorts</a> company.<sup id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Manhattan_developments">Manhattan developments</span></h4>
<p>Trump attracted public attention in 1978 with the launch of his family's first Manhattan venture, the renovation of the derelict <a href="/wiki/Grand_Hyatt_New_York" class="mw-redirect" title="Grand Hyatt New York">Commodore Hotel</a>, adjacent to <a href="/wiki/Grand_Central_Terminal" title="Grand Central Terminal">Grand Central Terminal</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup> The financing was facilitated by a $400&#160;million city property tax abatement arranged by Fred Trump,<sup id="cite_ref-Rich_NYMag_51-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rich_NYMag-51">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup> who also, jointly with Hyatt, guaranteed a $70&#160;million in bank construction financing.<sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup> The hotel reopened in 1980 as the <a href="/wiki/Grand_Hyatt_New_York" class="mw-redirect" title="Grand Hyatt New York">Grand Hyatt Hotel</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA84_84&#93;_56-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA84_84]-56">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup> and that same year, Trump obtained rights to develop <a href="/wiki/Trump_Tower" title="Trump Tower">Trump Tower</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Mixed-use_development" title="Mixed-use development">mixed-use</a> skyscraper in <a href="/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan" title="Midtown Manhattan">Midtown Manhattan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> The building houses the headquarters of the Trump Corporation and Trump's <a href="/wiki/Political_action_committee" title="Political action committee">PAC</a> and was Trump's primary residence until 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-moved_59-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-moved-59">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1988, Trump acquired the Plaza Hotel with a loan from a consortium of banks.<sup id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup> The hotel filed for bankruptcy protection in 1992, and a reorganization plan was approved a month later.<sup id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup> In 1995, Trump sold the Plaza Hotel along with most of his properties to pay down his debts, including personally guaranteed loans, allowing him to avoid personal bankruptcy.<sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1996, Trump acquired the mostly vacant 71-story skyscraper at <a href="/wiki/40_Wall_Street" title="40 Wall Street">40 Wall Street</a>, later rebranded as the Trump Building, and renovated it.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidLqf0CwAAQBAJpgPA298_298&#93;_64-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidLqf0CwAAQBAJpgPA298_298]-64">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup> In the early 1990s, Trump won the right to develop a 70-acre (28&#160;ha) tract in the <a href="/wiki/Lincoln_Square,_Manhattan" title="Lincoln Square, Manhattan">Lincoln Square</a> neighborhood near the <a href="/wiki/Hudson_River" title="Hudson River">Hudson River</a>. Struggling with debt from other ventures in 1994, Trump sold most of his interest in the project to Asian investors, who were able to finance the project's completion, <a href="/wiki/Riverside_South,_Manhattan" title="Riverside South, Manhattan">Riverside South</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Atlantic_City_casinos">Atlantic City casinos</span></h4>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Trump_Taj_Mahal,_2007.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="The entrance of the Trump Taj Mahal, a casino in Atlantic City. It has motifs evocative of the Taj Mahal in India." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Trump_Taj_Mahal%2C_2007.jpg/220px-Trump_Taj_Mahal%2C_2007.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Trump_Taj_Mahal%2C_2007.jpg/330px-Trump_Taj_Mahal%2C_2007.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Trump_Taj_Mahal%2C_2007.jpg/440px-Trump_Taj_Mahal%2C_2007.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944" /></a><figcaption>Entrance of the <a href="/wiki/Trump_Taj_Mahal" class="mw-redirect" title="Trump Taj Mahal">Trump Taj Mahal</a> in <a href="/wiki/Atlantic_City" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlantic City">Atlantic City</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1984, Trump opened <a href="/wiki/Harrah%27s_at_Trump_Plaza" class="mw-redirect" title="Harrah&#39;s at Trump Plaza">Harrah's at Trump Plaza</a>, a hotel and casino, with financing and management help from the <a href="/wiki/Holiday_Corporation" class="mw-redirect" title="Holiday Corporation">Holiday Corporation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-fall_66-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fall-66">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup> It was unprofitable, and Trump paid Holiday $70&#160;million in May 1986 to take sole control.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA128_128&#93;_67-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA128_128]-67">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup> In 1985, Trump bought the unopened Atlantic City Hilton Hotel and renamed it <a href="/wiki/Golden_Nugget_Atlantic_City" title="Golden Nugget Atlantic City">Trump Castle</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup> His wife Ivana managed it until 1988.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA137_137&#93;_69-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA137_137]-69">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup> Both casinos filed for <a href="/wiki/Chapter_11" class="mw-redirect" title="Chapter 11">Chapter 11</a> bankruptcy protection in 1992.<sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Trump bought a third Atlantic City venue in 1988, the <a href="/wiki/Hard_Rock_Hotel_%26_Casino_Atlantic_City" title="Hard Rock Hotel &amp; Casino Atlantic City">Trump Taj Mahal</a>. It was financed with $675&#160;million in <a href="/wiki/Junk_bonds" class="mw-redirect" title="Junk bonds">junk bonds</a> and completed for $1.1&#160;billion, opening in April 1990.<sup id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-71">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA135_135&#93;_72-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA135_135]-72">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup> Trump filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 1991. Under the provisions of the restructuring agreement, Trump gave up half his initial stake and personally guaranteed future performance.<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup> To reduce his $900&#160;million of personal debt, he sold the <a href="/wiki/Trump_Shuttle" title="Trump Shuttle">Trump Shuttle</a> airline; his <a href="/wiki/Megayacht" class="mw-redirect" title="Megayacht">megayacht</a>, the <i><a href="/wiki/Trump_Princess" class="mw-redirect" title="Trump Princess">Trump Princess</a></i>, which had been leased to his casinos and kept docked; and other businesses.<sup id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1995, Trump founded Trump Hotels &amp; Casino Resorts (THCR), which assumed ownership of the Trump Plaza.<sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup> THCR purchased the Taj Mahal and the <a href="/wiki/Trump_Castle" class="mw-redirect" title="Trump Castle">Trump Castle</a> in 1996 and went bankrupt in 2004 and 2009, leaving Trump with 10 percent ownership.<sup id="cite_ref-fall_66-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fall-66">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup> He remained chairman until 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Mar-a-Lago">Mar-a-Lago</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Mar-a-Lago" title="Mar-a-Lago">Mar-a-Lago</a></div>
<p>In 1985, Trump acquired the Mar-a-Lago estate in <a href="/wiki/Palm_Beach,_Florida" title="Palm Beach, Florida">Palm Beach, Florida</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup> In 1995, he converted the estate into a private club with an initiation fee and annual dues. He continued to use a wing of the house as a private residence.<sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> In 2019, Trump declared Mar-a-Lago his primary residence.<sup id="cite_ref-moved_59-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-moved-59">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Golf_courses">Golf courses</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump_and_golf" title="Donald Trump and golf">Donald Trump and golf</a></div>
<p>The Trump Organization began building and buying golf courses in 1999.<sup id="cite_ref-CNN_79-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNN-79">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> It owns fourteen and manages another three Trump-branded courses worldwide.<sup id="cite_ref-CNN_79-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNN-79">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Trump visited a Trump Organization property on 428 (nearly one in three) of the 1,461 days of his presidency and is estimated to have played 261 rounds of golf, one every 5.6 days.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81">&#91;80&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Licensing_of_the_Trump_brand">Licensing of the Trump brand</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_things_named_after_Donald_Trump" title="List of things named after Donald Trump">List of things named after Donald Trump</a></div>
<p>The Trump name has been licensed for various consumer products and services, including foodstuffs, apparel, <a href="/wiki/Trump_Institute" title="Trump Institute">adult learning courses</a>, and home furnishings.<sup id="cite_ref-neckties_82-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-neckties-82">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83">&#91;82&#93;</a></sup> According to an analysis by <i><a href="/wiki/The_Washington_Post" title="The Washington Post">The Washington Post</a></i>, there are more than 50 licensing or management deals involving Trump's name, and they have generated at least $59&#160;million in revenue for his companies.<sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup> By 2018, only two consumer goods companies continued to license his name.<sup id="cite_ref-neckties_82-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-neckties-82">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Side_ventures">Side ventures</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Trump, Doug Flutie, and an unnamed official standing behind a lectern with big, round New Jersey Generals sign, with members of the press seated in the background" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg/260px-Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg" decoding="async" width="260" height="177" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg/390px-Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg/520px-Donald_Trump_and_Doug_Flutie_at_a_press_conference_in_the_Trump_Tower.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4916" data-file-height="3344" /></a><figcaption>Trump and New Jersey Generals quarterback <a href="/wiki/Doug_Flutie" title="Doug Flutie">Doug Flutie</a> at a 1985 press conference in the lobby of Trump Tower</figcaption></figure>
<p>In September 1983, Trump purchased the <a href="/wiki/New_Jersey_Generals" title="New Jersey Generals">New Jersey Generals</a>, a team in the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Football_League" title="United States Football League">United States Football League</a>. After the 1985 season, the league folded, largely due to Trump's strategy of moving games to a fall schedule (when they competed with the <a href="/wiki/NFL" class="mw-redirect" title="NFL">NFL</a> for audience) and trying to force a merger with the NFL by bringing an <a href="/wiki/United_States_antitrust_law" title="United States antitrust law">antitrust suit</a> against the organization.<sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85">&#91;84&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Trump's businesses have hosted several boxing matches at the <a href="/wiki/Boardwalk_Hall" title="Boardwalk Hall">Atlantic City Convention Hall</a>, adjacent to and promoted as taking place at the Trump Plaza in Atlantic City.<sup id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87">&#91;86&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEO&#39;DonnellRutherford1991137_88-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO&#39;DonnellRutherford1991137-88">&#91;87&#93;</a></sup> In 1989 and 1990, Trump lent his name to the <a href="/wiki/Tour_de_Trump" class="mw-redirect" title="Tour de Trump">Tour de Trump</a> cycling stage race, which was an attempt to create an American equivalent of European races such as the <a href="/wiki/Tour_de_France" title="Tour de France">Tour de France</a> or the <a href="/wiki/Giro_d%27Italia" title="Giro d&#39;Italia">Giro d'Italia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>From 1986 to 1988, Trump purchased significant blocks of shares in various public companies while <a href="/wiki/Corporate_raid" title="Corporate raid">suggesting that he intended to take over</a> the company and then sold his shares for a profit,<sup id="cite_ref-Buettner-190508_45-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buettner-190508-45">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> leading some observers to think he was engaged in <a href="/wiki/Greenmail" title="Greenmail">greenmail</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90">&#91;89&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</a></i> found that Trump initially made millions of dollars in such stock transactions, but later "lost most, if not all, of those gains after investors stopped taking his takeover talk seriously".<sup id="cite_ref-Buettner-190508_45-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buettner-190508-45">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1988, Trump purchased the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Air_Lines_Shuttle" title="Eastern Air Lines Shuttle">Eastern Air Lines Shuttle</a>, financing the purchase with $380&#160;million (equivalent to $940&#160;million in 2022)<sup id="cite_ref-inflation-US_33-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inflation-US-33">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> in loans from a syndicate of 22 banks. He renamed the airline <a href="/wiki/Trump_Shuttle" title="Trump Shuttle">Trump Shuttle</a> and operated it until 1992.<sup id="cite_ref-TA_91-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TA-91">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup> Trump defaulted on his loans in 1991, and ownership passed to the banks.<sup id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup> The airline was eventually sold to US Airways.<sup id="cite_ref-TA_91-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TA-91">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1992, Trump, his siblings <a href="/wiki/Maryanne_Trump_Barry" title="Maryanne Trump Barry">Maryanne</a>, Elizabeth, and <a href="/wiki/Robert_Trump" title="Robert Trump">Robert</a>, and his cousin John W. Walter, each with a 20 percent share, formed All County Building Supply &amp; Maintenance Corp. The company had no offices and is alleged to have been a shell company for paying the vendors providing services and supplies for Trump's rental units, then billing those services and supplies to Trump Management with markups of 20–50 percent and more. The owners shared the proceeds generated by the markups.<sup id="cite_ref-Tax_Schemes_41-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tax_Schemes-41">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-93">&#91;92&#93;</a></sup> The increased costs were used as justification to get state approval for increasing the rents of Trump's rent-stabilized units.<sup id="cite_ref-Tax_Schemes_41-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tax_Schemes-41">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="A red star with a bronze outline and &quot;Donald Trump&quot; and a TV icon written on it in bronze, embedded in a black terrazzo sidewalk" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG/150px-Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG" decoding="async" width="150" height="120" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG/225px-Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG/300px-Donald_Trump_star_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2843" data-file-height="2282" /></a><figcaption>Trump's star on the <a href="/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame" title="Hollywood Walk of Fame">Hollywood Walk of Fame</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>From 1996 to 2015, Trump owned all or part of the <a href="/wiki/Miss_Universe" title="Miss Universe">Miss Universe</a> pageants, including <a href="/wiki/Miss_USA" title="Miss USA">Miss USA</a> and <a href="/wiki/Miss_Teen_USA" title="Miss Teen USA">Miss Teen USA</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-pageantsaleWME_94-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pageantsaleWME-94">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup> Due to disagreements with <a href="/wiki/CBS" title="CBS">CBS</a> about scheduling, he took both pageants to <a href="/wiki/NBC" title="NBC">NBC</a> in 2002.<sup id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-96">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-97" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-97">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup> In 2007, Trump received a star on the <a href="/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame" title="Hollywood Walk of Fame">Hollywood Walk of Fame</a> for his work as producer of Miss Universe.<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup> NBC and <a href="/wiki/Univision" title="Univision">Univision</a> dropped the pageants from their broadcasting lineups in June 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Trump_University">Trump University</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Trump_University" title="Trump University">Trump University</a></div>
<p>In 2004, Trump co-founded <a href="/wiki/Trump_University" title="Trump University">Trump University</a>, a company that sold real-estate training courses priced from $1,500 to $35,000.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup> After New York State authorities notified the company that its use of the word "university" violated state law (as it was not an academic institution), its name was changed to the Trump Entrepreneur Initiative in 2010.<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2013, the State of New York filed a $40&#160;million civil suit against Trump University, alleging that the company made false statements and defrauded consumers.<sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup> In addition, two <a href="/wiki/Class_action" title="Class action">class actions</a> were filed in federal court against Trump and his companies. Internal documents revealed that employees were instructed to use a hard-sell approach, and former employees testified that Trump University had defrauded or lied to its students.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-104">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-105">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup> Shortly after he won the 2016 presidential election, Trump agreed to pay a total of $25&#160;million to settle the three cases.<sup id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-106">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foundation">Foundation</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Donald_J._Trump_Foundation" title="Donald J. Trump Foundation">Donald J. Trump Foundation</a></div>
<p>The Donald J. Trump Foundation was a <a href="/wiki/Private_foundation_(United_States)" title="Private foundation (United States)">private foundation</a> established in 1988.<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup> In the foundation's final years, its funds mostly came from donors other than Trump, who did not donate any personal funds to the charity from 2009 until 2014.<sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup> The foundation gave to health-care- and sports-related charities, as well as conservative groups.<sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2016, <i>The Washington Post</i> reported that the charity committed several potential legal and ethical violations, including alleged self-dealing and possible <a href="/wiki/Tax_evasion" title="Tax evasion">tax evasion</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup> Also in 2016, the <a href="/wiki/New_York_Attorney_General" class="mw-redirect" title="New York Attorney General">New York Attorney General</a> determined the foundation to be in violation of state law for soliciting donations and ordered it to immediately cease its fundraising activities in New York.<sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup> Trump's team announced in December 2016 that the foundation would be dissolved.<sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In June 2018, the New York attorney general's office filed a civil suit against the foundation, Trump, and his adult children, seeking $2.8&#160;million in restitution and additional penalties.<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-115" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-115">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> In December 2018, the foundation ceased operation and disbursed its assets to other charities.<sup id="cite_ref-116" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-116">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup> In November 2019, a New York state judge ordered Trump to pay $2&#160;million to a group of charities for misusing the foundation's funds, in part to finance his presidential campaign.<sup id="cite_ref-117" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-117">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Legal_affairs_and_bankruptcies">Legal affairs and bankruptcies</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Legal_affairs_of_Donald_Trump" class="mw-redirect" title="Legal affairs of Donald Trump">Legal affairs of Donald Trump</a></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Roy_Cohn" title="Roy Cohn">Roy Cohn</a> was Trump's <a href="/wiki/Fixer_(person)" title="Fixer (person)">fixer</a>, lawyer, and mentor for 13 years in the 1970s and 1980s.<sup id="cite_ref-Mahler2016Cohn_119-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mahler2016Cohn-119">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup> According to Trump, Cohn sometimes waived fees due to their friendship.<sup id="cite_ref-Mahler2016Cohn_119-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mahler2016Cohn-119">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup> In 1973, Cohn helped Trump countersue the United States government for $100&#160;million (equivalent to $659&#160;million in 2022)<sup id="cite_ref-inflation-US_33-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inflation-US-33">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> over its charges that Trump's properties had racial discriminatory practices. Trump's counterclaims were dismissed, and the government's case went forward, ultimately resulting in a settlement.<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> In 1975, an agreement was struck requiring Trump's properties to furnish the <a href="/wiki/National_Urban_League" title="National Urban League">New York Urban League</a> with a list of all apartment vacancies, every week for two years, among other things.<sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup> Cohn introduced political consultant <a href="/wiki/Roger_Stone" title="Roger Stone">Roger Stone</a> to Trump, who enlisted Stone's services to deal with the federal government.<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to a review of state and federal court files conducted by <i><a href="/wiki/USA_Today" title="USA Today">USA Today</a></i> in 2018, Trump and his businesses had been involved in more than 4,000 state and federal legal actions.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup> While Trump has not filed for <a href="/wiki/Personal_bankruptcy" title="Personal bankruptcy">personal bankruptcy</a>, his over-leveraged hotel and casino businesses in Atlantic City and New York filed for <a href="/wiki/Chapter_11_bankruptcy" class="mw-redirect" title="Chapter 11 bankruptcy">Chapter 11 bankruptcy</a> protection six times between 1991 and 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-TW_124-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TW-124">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup> They continued to operate while the banks restructured debt and reduced Trump's shares in the properties.<sup id="cite_ref-TW_124-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TW-124">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During the 1980s, more than 70 banks had lent Trump $4&#160;billion.<sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup> After his corporate bankruptcies of the early 1990s most major banks, with the exception of Deutsche Bank, declined to lend to him.<sup id="cite_ref-126" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-126">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup> After the <a href="/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack" title="January 6 United States Capitol attack">January 6 United States Capitol attack</a>, the bank decided not to do business with Trump or his company in the future.<sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Media_career">Media career</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Media_career_of_Donald_Trump" title="Media career of Donald Trump">Media career of Donald Trump</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Books">Books</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Bibliography_of_Donald_Trump" title="Bibliography of Donald Trump">Bibliography of Donald Trump</a></div>
<p>Using <a href="/wiki/Ghostwriters" class="mw-redirect" title="Ghostwriters">ghostwriters</a>, Trump has produced up to 19 books on business, financial, or political topics under his name.<sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup> His first book, <i><a href="/wiki/The_Art_of_the_Deal" class="mw-redirect" title="The Art of the Deal">The Art of the Deal</a></i> (1987), was a <a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list" title="The New York Times Best Seller list"><i>New York Times</i> Best Seller</a>. While Trump was credited as co-author, the entire book was written by <a href="/wiki/Tony_Schwartz_(author)" title="Tony Schwartz (author)">Tony Schwartz</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-MayerGhost_129-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MayerGhost-129">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> According to <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_Yorker" title="The New Yorker">The New Yorker</a></i>, "The book expanded Trump's renown far beyond New York City, making him an emblem of the successful tycoon."<sup id="cite_ref-MayerGhost_129-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MayerGhost-129">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> Trump has called the volume his second favorite book, after the Bible.<sup id="cite_ref-130" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-130">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Film_and_television">Film and television</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Media_career_of_Donald_Trump" title="Media career of Donald Trump">Media career of Donald Trump</a></div>
<p>Trump made <a href="/wiki/Cameo_appearances" class="mw-redirect" title="Cameo appearances">cameo appearances</a> in many films and television shows from 1985 to 2001.<sup id="cite_ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Trump had a sporadic relationship with the <a href="/wiki/Professional_wrestling" title="Professional wrestling">professional wrestling</a> promotion <a href="/wiki/WWE" title="WWE">WWE</a> since the late 1980s.<sup id="cite_ref-132" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-132">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup> He appeared at <a href="/wiki/WrestleMania_23" title="WrestleMania 23">WrestleMania 23</a> in 2007 and was inducted into the celebrity wing of the <a href="/wiki/WWE_Hall_of_Fame_(2013)" title="WWE Hall of Fame (2013)">WWE Hall of Fame in 2013</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_trump_at_the_game_(3728975319).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Trump, in a suit, sits in a crowded baseball stadium" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Donald_trump_at_the_game_%283728975319%29.jpg/200px-Donald_trump_at_the_game_%283728975319%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="136" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Donald_trump_at_the_game_%283728975319%29.jpg/300px-Donald_trump_at_the_game_%283728975319%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Donald_trump_at_the_game_%283728975319%29.jpg/400px-Donald_trump_at_the_game_%283728975319%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="642" data-file-height="435" /></a><figcaption>Trump at a <a href="/wiki/New_York_Mets" title="New York Mets">New York Mets</a> baseball game in 2009</figcaption></figure>
<p>Starting in the 1990s, Trump was a guest about 24 times on the nationally syndicated <i><a href="/wiki/Howard_Stern_Show" class="mw-redirect" title="Howard Stern Show">Howard Stern Show</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017&#91;httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA166_166&#93;_134-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher2017[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidx2jUDQAAQBAJpgPA166_166]-134">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup> He also had his own short-form talk radio program called <i><a href="/wiki/Trumped!" title="Trumped!">Trumped!</a></i> (one to two minutes on weekdays) from 2004 to 2008.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-136" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-136">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> From 2011 until 2015, he was a weekly unpaid guest commentator on <i><a href="/wiki/Fox_%26_Friends" title="Fox &amp; Friends">Fox &amp; Friends</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>From 2004 to 2015, Trump was co-producer and host of reality shows <i>The Apprentice</i> and <i><a href="/wiki/The_Celebrity_Apprentice" title="The Celebrity Apprentice">The Celebrity Apprentice</a></i>. On <i>The Apprentice</i>, Trump played the role of a chief executive, and contestants competed for a year of employment at the Trump Organization. On <i>The Celebrity Apprentice</i>, celebrities competed to win money for charities. On both shows, Trump eliminated contestants with the <a href="/wiki/Catchphrase" title="Catchphrase">catchphrase</a> "You're fired."<sup id="cite_ref-born_7-17-16_139-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-born_7-17-16-139">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In February 2021, Trump resigned from the <a href="/wiki/SAG-AFTRA" title="SAG-AFTRA">Screen Actors Guild</a> he had been a member of since 1989 rather than face a disciplinary committee hearing for inciting the January 6, 2021, mob attack on the U.S. Capitol and for his "reckless campaign of misinformation aimed at discrediting and ultimately threatening the safety of journalists".<sup id="cite_ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup> Two days later, the union permanently barred him from readmission.<sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Political_career">Political career</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Political_career_of_Donald_Trump" title="Political career of Donald Trump">Political career of Donald Trump</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Donald Trump shakes hands with Bill Clinton in a lobby; Trump is speaking and Clinton is smiling, and both are wearing suits." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg/220px-Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg/330px-Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg/440px-Donald_Trump_and_Bill_Clinton.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2560" data-file-height="1707" /></a><figcaption>Trump and President <a href="/wiki/Bill_Clinton" title="Bill Clinton">Bill Clinton</a> in June 2000</figcaption></figure>
<p>Trump's political party affiliation has changed numerous times. He registered as a Republican in 1987;<sup id="cite_ref-reg_142-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reg-142">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup> a member of the <a href="/wiki/Independence_Party_of_New_York" title="Independence Party of New York">Independence Party</a>, the New York state affiliate of the <a href="/wiki/Reform_Party_of_the_United_States_of_America" title="Reform Party of the United States of America">Reform Party</a>, in 1999;<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> a Democrat in 2001; a Republican in 2009; unaffiliated in 2011; and a Republican in 2012.<sup id="cite_ref-reg_142-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reg-142">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1987, Trump placed full-page advertisements in three major newspapers,<sup id="cite_ref-hint_144-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hint-144">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup> expressing his views on foreign policy and on how to eliminate the federal budget deficit.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> He ruled out running for local office but not for the presidency.<sup id="cite_ref-hint_144-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hint-144">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup> In 1988, he approached <a href="/wiki/Lee_Atwater" title="Lee Atwater">Lee Atwater</a>, asking to be put into consideration to be Republican nominee <a href="/wiki/George_H._W._Bush" title="George H. W. Bush">George H. W. Bush</a>'s running mate. Bush found the request "strange and unbelievable".<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="Presidential_campaigns_.282000.E2.80.932016.29"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Presidential_campaigns_(2000–2016)">Presidential campaigns (2000–2016)</span></h3>
<p>In 2000, Trump <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump_2000_presidential_campaign" title="Donald Trump 2000 presidential campaign">ran in the California and Michigan primaries</a> for nomination as the Reform Party candidate for the <a href="/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election" title="2000 United States presidential election">2000 United States presidential election</a> but withdrew from the race in February 2000.<sup id="cite_ref-147" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-147">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> A July 1999 poll matching him against likely Republican nominee <a href="/wiki/George_W._Bush" title="George W. Bush">George W. Bush</a> and likely Democratic nominee <a href="/wiki/Al_Gore" title="Al Gore">Al Gore</a> showed Trump with seven percent support.<sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Trump, leaning heavily onto a lectern, with his mouth open mid-speech and a woman clapping politely next to him" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg/220px-Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg/330px-Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg/440px-Donald_Trump_speaking_at_CPAC_2011_by_Mark_Taylor.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456" /></a><figcaption>Trump speaking at <a href="/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference" title="Conservative Political Action Conference">CPAC</a> 2011</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2011, Trump <a href="/wiki/Barack_Obama_citizenship_conspiracy_theories#Donald_Trump" title="Barack Obama citizenship conspiracy theories">speculated about running</a> against President Barack Obama in <a href="/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election" title="2012 United States presidential election">the 2012 election</a>, making his first speaking appearance at the <a href="/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference" title="Conservative Political Action Conference">Conservative Political Action Conference</a> (CPAC) in February 2011 and giving speeches in early primary states.<sup id="cite_ref-McA_151-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-McA-151">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> In May 2011, he announced he would not run,<sup id="cite_ref-McA_151-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-McA-151">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup> and he endorsed <a href="/wiki/Mitt_Romney" title="Mitt Romney">Mitt Romney</a> in February 2012.<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> Trump's presidential ambitions were generally not taken seriously at the time.<sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="2016_presidential_campaign">2016 presidential campaign</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump_2016_presidential_campaign" title="Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign">Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/2016_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries" title="2016 Republican Party presidential primaries">2016 Republican Party presidential primaries</a> and <a href="/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election#General_election_campaign" title="2016 United States presidential election">2016 United States presidential election §&#160;General election campaign</a></div>
<p>Trump's fame and provocative statements earned him an unprecedented amount of <a href="/wiki/Earned_media" title="Earned media">free media coverage</a>, elevating his standing in the Republican primaries.<sup id="cite_ref-Cillizza-160614_155-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Cillizza-160614-155">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> He adopted the phrase "truthful hyperbole", coined by his ghostwriter Tony Schwartz, to describe his public speaking style.<sup id="cite_ref-MayerGhost_129-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MayerGhost-129">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> His campaign statements were often opaque and suggestive,<sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup> and a record number of them were false.<sup id="cite_ref-whoppers_158-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-whoppers-158">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> The <i><a href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times" title="Los Angeles Times">Los Angeles Times</a></i> wrote, "Never in modern presidential politics has a major candidate made false statements as routinely as Trump has."<sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-finnegan_162-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-finnegan-162">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> Trump said he disdained <a href="/wiki/Political_correctness" title="Political correctness">political correctness</a> and frequently made claims of <a href="/wiki/Media_bias" title="Media bias">media bias</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Walsh-160724_163-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Walsh-160724-163">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Trump speaking in front of an American flag behind a lectern, wearing a black suit and red hat. The lectern sports a blue &quot;TRUMP&quot; sign." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg/220px-Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg/330px-Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg/440px-Donald_Trump_by_Gage_Skidmore_5.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4272" data-file-height="2848" /></a><figcaption>Trump campaigning in Arizona, March 2016</figcaption></figure>
